clue.text: Extolling merits of goat as an old means of conveyance

parts.note: puffing something is praising it extravagantly, as in a puff for a book
a billy is a male goat

explanation.surface: Someone sings the praises of a goat as a handy way of getting about in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: Puffing Billy was one of the earliest steam locomotives, built in 1813 for a colliery in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic engine of that name is an early railway locomotive, a vehicle from transport's distant past.

clue.text: Little dog is said to be British down under

indicators.note: said signals that the words before it are spoken rather than written

parts.note: a pom is a Pomeranian, a small dog breed, so this phrase becomes pom is

explanation.surface: A remark that a small dog counts as British in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray apostrophe after 'Little' is an OCR mark; the page prints plain 'Little'. Pommies is Australian slang for British people.
explanation.definitionFit: Australians and New Zealanders use this slang term for English or British people.

clue.text: Was wont to follow football's leader — United

indicators.note: follow places the second piece after the first
the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of football's

parts.note: was wont to means used to, habitually did

explanation.surface: A team habitually trailed behind the top football club, United.
explanation.definitionFit: Things joined together into one have become united, melted or merged.

clue.text: Hence life among the shell-bursts in a West Indian high spot

parts.note: taken as written
Cuba is a West Indian island
a tor is a rocky hill peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone survives shellfire on a Caribbean hilltop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: chicks emerge from cracked shells in this warm box, so life comes from it among bursting shells, not artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated hatching apparatus is where eggs break open and new life appears.

clue.text: A Dickensian bird in. one's hand-luggage?

definitions.meaning: the talking raven owned by Barnaby Rudge in Dickens's novel
a travelling bag carried by hand

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens named Barnaby Rudge's raven this, and the word is also an old term for a holdall.

clue.text: One held by this strange man in these games

indicators.note: held by puts the first piece inside the letters of the rearranged words
strange tells us the words this man are jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is gripped by an odd fellow taking part in some sports event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' places the single letter inside the jumbled words, which 'strange' signals; the games were named after the Isthmus of Corinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isthmian Games were ancient Greek athletic contests held at Corinth, on its isthmus.

clue.text: All flat either way

indicators.note: either way says the letters read the same forwards or backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Everything is flat whichever direction you look.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface that is flat throughout is even, with no rise or fall.

clue.text: Member getting academic appointment as such as critic …

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a chair is a professorship at a university

explanation.surface: A member of staff wins a professorship and so becomes a critic.
explanation.walkthrough: An armchair critic judges from comfort without practical experience; the ellipsis runs on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical, from-the-sofa criticism is described with this word, as in an armchair general.

clue.text: … prevailed over Edward as usual

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: prevailed means won
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone triumphed over a man named Edward, as is customary.
explanation.definitionFit: Wonted means customary or habitual, the way things normally are.

clue.text: A glutton for punishment, he takes pigfeed outside a Black Sea resort

indicators.note: outside means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak that pigs eat
Sochi is a Russian resort on the Black Sea

explanation.surface: A man who loves suffering brings pig food to a seaside holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who enjoys pain or hardship is a sucker for suffering.

clue.text: Astraea as lion-chaser

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth the star maiden Astraea was placed in the sky as the constellation of the Virgin
in the zodiac the sign of the Virgin comes straight after Leo, the lion

explanation.definitionFit: Myth makes the goddess of justice into this constellation, and in the zodiac it follows Leo.

clue.text: In which we find a Bantu tribal conference

indicators.note: In which we find tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Bantu tribe is found inside some gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Indaba is a Zulu word for a council or meeting of tribal elders in southern Africa.

clue.text: One St Stephen's man following the law without reservation

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
St Stephen's is an old name for the Houses of Parliament, so its man is an MP
licit means lawful, in line with the law

explanation.surface: A single Member of Parliament obeys the law completely.
explanation.walkthrough: St Stephen's Hall at Westminster gave Parliament this old nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit trust is absolute and unquestioning, given with no doubts held back.

clue.text: Inadequate container for worms in a filthy environment

indicators.note: in places the container inside the dirty surroundings

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a byword for filth
a can of worms, a tin for an angler's bait

explanation.surface: A tin of bait sits in a dirty place and is not good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre, insufficient in amount.

clue.text: Germans have this way to make — a high-class bath, no trouble

parts.note: U is the old label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: trouble means stir up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A recipe for a posh bath without fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' acts on A, U, BATH and NO, rearranging them.
explanation.definitionFit: German motorways are a road system famous for having no general speed limit.

clue.text: Constructed, say, by a workman, or a female servant

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: constructed means made

explanation.surface: Something is built by a labourer, or perhaps by a maidservant.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand-made is what a workman's product is; the second part is then spelt as the servant word that sounds like 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handmaid is a personal maid or woman attendant.

clue.text: Those going places may take courses in this

definitions.text: Those going places may take courses in this

parts.words: Those going places may take courses in this
parts.note: travellers eat meals course by course in a railway carriage, not study courses for ambitious people

explanation.definitionFit: Train passengers eat restaurant meals in this railway carriage.

clue.text: Old Dutchman was one-flying by night, like a bird

parts.note: a bat flies at night
avian means of or like birds

explanation.surface: An old Dutch fellow was a nocturnal flier, birdlike.
explanation.walkthrough: The Batavi were a Germanic tribe in the Rhine delta, so 'Batavian' is an old word for Dutch.
explanation.definitionFit: Batavia was the Latin name for Holland, so its people were called this.

clue.text: Stuff that's relevant

definitions.meaning: fabric or substance, the matter something is made of
pertinent, bearing on the matter at hand

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cloth or matter and significant or pertinent evidence.

clue.text: Married without love Mariana languished in this grange

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: mated means paired or married
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Wed but loveless, Mariana pined away in her country house.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's 'Mariana' wastes away in 'the moated grange'. 'without' looks like a minus but means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's poem places its lonely heroine in a farmhouse ringed by a ditch of water.

clue.text: A northern spruce found in Northern Ireland

parts.note: spruce means neat and smart, trim

explanation.surface: A northern conifer grows in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruce' looks like the tree but is the adjective meaning smart. Antrim is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This county lies in the north-east of Ulster, part of the province.

clue.text: Possibly represented as Times artist

indicators.note: possibly represented hints the letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A painter may have been depicted in this newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French painter, leader of the Fauves.

clue.text: A rook stood by a lake among the trees

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
stood in the sense of endured or tolerated, bore

explanation.surface: A crow perched beside a lake in a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Arboreal describes life in or among trees, like a squirrel's.

clue.text: After Twickenham game doctor goes to a dance

parts.note: Twickenham is the home of English rugby, so the game is RU, rugby union
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree

explanation.surface: After a rugby match the medic heads off to a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham, in south-west London, is England's national rugby stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Man on board not always as black as he sounds

indicators.note: as he sounds tells us the piece's word is heard as the answer

parts.note: night is black, the dark hours

explanation.surface: A chess piece is not always as dark as its name suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: Chessmen come in black and white, so this piece is only sometimes black like the night it sounds like.
explanation.definitionFit: A chess piece is a man on a board, and this one moves in an L-shape.

clue.text: Cold as some eels are said to be

indicators.note: said to be signals a word heard rather than written

parts.note: jellied eels are a traditional East London dish

explanation.surface: Some eels are reportedly chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels, eels set in their own jelly, are a London East End food.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid means icy, frozen.

clue.text: Hairdresser providing tea-time spread at Grantchester?

definitions.meaning: a toothed tool that dresses hair
Rupert Brooke's poem about Grantchester ends asking if there is honey still for tea

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hair-grooming tool and also the wax cells honey is served in.

clue.text: Say a flood survivor near Runnymede.

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
Ham was one of Noah's sons, who survived the Flood in the ark

explanation.surface: Someone survived a flood close to where Magna Carta was sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: Egham is a Surrey town beside Runnymede, the meadow on the Thames where Magna Carta was sealed in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: This Surrey town lies just by the historic riverside meadow.

clue.text: Leaders of 14, 21 and 22 are in a position to form such a triangle

definitions.text: Leaders of 14, 21 and 22 are in a position to form such a triangle

parts.words: Leaders of 14, 21 and 22 are in a position to form such a triangle
parts.note: the first letters of three entries sit in the grid at points making a triangle with two equal sides

explanation.surface: Three grid entries' starting squares mark out a particular kind of triangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle with two sides of equal length has this name.

clue.text: Bungay barred craftily by 4's master

indicators.note: craftily suggests the letters are cunningly rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was banned from the Suffolk town of Bungay by a cunning owner of a raven.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is GRIP, the raven owned by the title character of Dickens's novel. Bungay is a town in Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's simple-minded hero keeps the pet raven named in the cross-referenced clue.
